summary: Variant redispatch to secondary model during staged canary due to orchestrator snapshot lag
description:
Issue summary: During a staged canary rollout for redwood-llama-7b-v2 in us-east, ~3% of BrightHealth AI traffic was unexpectedly routed to the secondary variant (quantized fallback) despite an explicit tenant model pin. Impact: customer reported mixed responses in production affecting 12 tenant sessions (chat flows). Symptoms observed at 09:21 UTC: inconsistent model outputs from the same session-id, and increased token latency (p50 -> p95).

High-level hypothesis: orchestrator snapshot application lag caused a partial control-plane commit where edge proxies had stale routing snapshots while the central router had already committed a canary weight update. This led to a redispatch path where requests that should have be pinned were re-evaluated by a reconciliation step and dispatched to the secondary variant.

Requested outcome: restore full pin coherence for affected tenant(s), identify root cause in orchestration snapshot propagation, and add guardrails to avoid redispatch during staged commits.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Trigger a staged canary rollout for redwood-llama-7b-v2 with a small traffic weight (5%) in us-east.
2) Simulate a brief orchestrator leader failover during commit window (kill leader API process for ~6s) to force snapshot re-application.
3) Send long-lived chat sessions with pinned model headers for a tenant and observe routing headers and model ids returned by edge proxies.
4) Notice that some requests with the pinned header are returned from the quantized variant and show different model-id in response metadata.
5) Reproduce using traffic mirror to replay customer traffic against staging cluster to validate behavior.

comments: Ava Chen (Support) [2026-03-12T10:03Z]: Customer observed mixed responses starting at ~09:20 UTC. Collecting session IDs and example payloads. Escalating to SRE and Orchestratorowners.

SRE (Priya Nair) [2026-03-12T10:17Z]: Early look suggests snapshot apply on orchestrator leader took 6.4s due to compaction GC. Edge nodes pulled older snapshot concurrently causing transient routing divergence. Repro steps drafted.

Mateo Alvarez (Assigned) [2026-03-12T11:02Z]: Running replay of affected session traffic on staging mirrored cluster to reproduce redispatch. Noted that reconciliation path triggers when commit_idx mismatch and session lease renewal coincides with healthprobe backoff.

BrightHealth (EMMA) [2026-03-12T11:26Z]: We saw 12 sessions with garbled summaries; thanks for the quick response. We need fix and mitigation — customer requests rollback to previous canary immediately if pin coherence cannot be guaranteed.

Priya Nair (SRE) [2026-03-12T13:40Z]: Mitigation performed: paused the canary rollout, increased snapshot propagate timeout, and added a temporary edge-side check to prefer control-plane pin header until snapshot commit confirmed. Monitoring for re-occurrence.

Mateo Alvarez (Engineering) [2026-03-13T08:12Z]: Patch landed to add a short-term reconciliation guard (PR linked). Next: follow-up to remove guard after we verify orchestration GC tuning and snapshot apply times are within threshold.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: orchestrator snapshot apply delay due to compaction/GC caused inconsistent commit_idx across control-plane replicas.
Hypothesis B: edge-proxy healthprobe backoff triggered reconnection which invoked a reconciliation flow that re-evaluates model pin and allowed fallback routing when commit metadata was ambiguous.

Finding: reproduce on staging by forcing leader restart during commit window; replication delay & edge pull of older snapshot leads to short window where reconciliation code path marks session lease expired and redispatches to fallback variant.
Metric evidence: commit_idx skew observed between leader and follower at time-of-incident (leader=4124, follower=4119). Snapshot pull latencies increased from baseline ~120ms to ~6.2s during event.
Risk note: behavior affects long-lived sessions that renew leases during commit windows; short-lived requests less likely to hit redispatch flow.

Next steps: tune snapshot compaction GC to avoid long pause, add commit-confirm handshake to edge to avoid reconciling pins while snapshot mismatch present, add unit/integration tests for staged canary under leader failover.
resolution: Mitigation applied on 2026-03-12: paused canary rollout and deployed edge guard to prefer explicit model_pin header until commit confirmation. Engineering landed a short-term patch to prevent reconciliation-triggered redispatch during commit_idx skew (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2891). Longer-term fix: orchestration GC tuning + commit-confirm handshake. Customer BrightHealth AI notified and will monitor for 72 hours; ticket will be closed after 72h with no regression.
notes: Runbook references: OPS/Canary-orchestrator (linked). Follow-up action: schedule postmortem and create a task to add integration test coverage for orchestrator failover during staged canary (INT ticket to be created).
